content:
Kiran: Heads-up — canary telemetry shows a small but consistent tail latency increase on IO-heavy profiles after PR #7275 landed. Not huge (2–4% p50->p95 shift) but reproducible on the redis-backed test. https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/7275

bench-bot: Automated canary run results attached: 
```
baseline (main) : p50=18ms p90=42ms p95=78ms p99=210ms
canary (post-7275): p50=19ms p90=45ms p95=82ms p99=228ms
diff:   +5.6% p50  +7.1% p90  +5.1% p95  +8.6% p99
throughput: steady at 750rps, mem delta +12MB/container
```

Maya: Thanks for the ping. Do we have flamegraphs or a quick profile to point at where the extra time is spent?

Kiran: I ran a quick perf — the extra time is centered in the IO scheduler path when inflight KV cache misses combine with the new batch windowing. Attaching the short trace (snippet below).

Kiran: ```
# simplified hotspots from local perf
  28% io_scheduler::dispatch
  17% rpc::send_read_request
  12% uv_loop_poll
  10% allocator::slice_wait
  8% kv_cache::on_miss
```

Rafael: That matches my local repro. The change in 7275 that widened the batching horizon is the likely culprit (it reduces cold microbatch rate but increases contention occasionally).

Jo: Can we A/B a small tweak? If we reduce the batch horizon from 12ms -> 8ms does p95 improve? If so we can ship a quick fix config and iterate.

Kiran: I ran that locally: horizon=8ms brings p95 back within 1% of baseline but p50 regresses slightly (~+1ms). I pushed a bench script to the PR comment which runs the same redis profile: `./bench/scripts/kv_longseq.sh --batch-horizon=8`

Maya: Sounds acceptable as a canary mitigation while we investigate the root cause more (we don't want tail increases in prod). Can we hold the canary rollout and patch the config?

deploy-bot: Canary rollout paused for PR 7275 as of 2026-03-16T15:12:02Z — reason: lat/regression-detected.

Kiran: I'll open a small follow-up PR (7276) that sets the default horizon to 8ms and marks the change as an opt-in via runtime flag. Requesting 1 reviewer snd + infra signoff.

Rafael: I'll review 7276 now. Quick glance: change looks straightforward, but please add a comment linking to the bench results and the canary run id.

Jo: If Rafael gives LGTM, can someone from infra approve the rollout change? It touches scheduling defaults.

Maya: cc @Rafael — after LGTM I'll ping infra and product for a brief note. Also let's add a small regression test in bench harness so the CI flags any p95 drift >3% in future canaries.

Kiran: Good idea — adding a lightweight assertion to bench-bot config now. Patch ETA ~20–30m.

bench-bot: Added regression guard: canary_regression_threshold: p95 > 3% will fail auto-rollout. PR updated.

Rafael: Reviewed 7276 — left one nit about the config comment. LGTM after that.

Kiran: Fixed nit, pushed. Requesting merge (needs infra 2nd).

Jo: I'll ping infra in #eng-infra and ask for a quick review and approval to merge + re-run canary.

Jo: @infra-team quick heads-up: PR 7276 reduces default batch horizon to 8ms as a canary mitigation for tail latency (linked bench results). Rafael reviewed; needs infra sign-off for scheduling default change.

Kiran: Thanks. Will hold on merging until infra clears and the bench-run passes.

Maya: Great coordination — let's aim to get the canary unblocked today if possible. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Canary re-run scheduled: id=canary-20260316-2 (blocked until infra approval).

Kiran: Follow-up note for post-mitigation root cause work: plan to instrument KV cache hit paths to capture queuing times, and run targeted microbench with synthetic miss bursts. Will open an RFC in eng-runtime for longer-term solution.

Rafael: Thanks all. If anything else pops on the canary runs I'll post numbers here.

Maya: If infra gives the green, we can merge and re-evaluate after one successful canary pass.

Kiran: Closing loop — infra approved and merged at 2026-03-16T15:34:00Z, canary re-run in progress. Will report final numbers when bench completes.

bench-bot: Final canary re-run results: p95 within +0.8% of baseline, p99 still +4% (low sample). Marking as pass per threshold.
